# AI Work Index

> AI displacement risk scores for 562 Singapore occupations and 88 modern roles, using a deterministic three-layer model (exposure, human bottleneck, market resilience). Open data, no LLMs in the pipeline.

## About

AI Work Index is a free, open-source tool that scores every major Singapore occupation for structural AI displacement risk. The model combines academic exposure indices (Felten AIOE, Anthropic Economic Index) with O*NET human-bottleneck data and Singapore-specific labour market signals (MOM wages, Shortage Occupation List, Jobs in Demand). Scores are structural pressure indicators, not predictions of actual job losses.

- Author: Kirill So
- Data vintage: V5, last updated 2026-03-30
- Coverage: 562 SSOC occupations + 88 synthetic modern roles
- Location focus: Singapore

## Scoring Formula

net_risk = AI_exposure x (1 - human_bottleneck) x market_modifier

- Exposure: Ensemble of Felten AIOE (50%) + Anthropic observed usage (50%)
- Bottleneck: Pizzinelli theta from O*NET work context (coordination, physical presence)
- Market modifier: Singapore employment trends, SOL 2026, Jobs in Demand 2025

- https://aiworkindex.com/rankings/ai-leveraged — Occupations most augmented by AI
- https://aiworkindex.com/rankings/safest-high-paying — High-paying, low-risk occupations
- https://aiworkindex.com/rankings/rich-and-risky — High-paying, high-risk occupations
- https://aiworkindex.com/reports/wage-exposure — SGD 46B wage exposure analysis
- https://aiworkindex.com/explore — Filter and visualize all occupations
- https://aiworkindex.com/compare — Side-by-side occupation comparison
- https://aiworkindex.com/calculator — Personalized salary vs AI risk calculator
- https://aiworkindex.com/about — Model card, data vintage, credits

## Risk Bands

| Band | Net Risk Range | Example |
|------|---------------|---------|
| Very Low | < 5% | Surgeons, Physiotherapists |
| Low | 5-15% | Civil Engineers, Dentists |
| Moderate | 15-30% | Marketing Managers, Journalists |
| High | 30-50% | Bookkeepers, Insurance Agents |
| Very High | >= 50% | Data Entry Clerks, Telemarketers |

## Key Research Citations

- Frank et al. (2025): ensemble exposure measures outperform single indices
- Acemoglu & Restrepo (2019): displacement vs reinstatement framework
- Stanford DEL (2025): entry-level workers face disproportionate displacement
- Brynjolfsson et al. (2023): junior workers see biggest AI productivity gains
- Brookings/PIIE (2026): AI labour impact "still in the first inning"
